title: Six LLMs trade $10k each live on crypto markets; only two finish in profit
summary: Nof1's Alpha Arena gave six frontier models $10,000 each to trade crypto perpetuals on Hyperliquid with no human intervention, a public test of LLMs as autonomous trading agents.
model: Qwen 3 Max, DeepSeek, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok, GPT-5
agent_role: Each model decided and executed its own trades on live markets; organizers set the prompts and rules and did not intervene during the season.
outcome: Qwen 3 Max finished first at $12,231 and DeepSeek second at $10,489; the other four models ended with large losses
what_they_did: Nof1.ai ran Alpha Arena Season 1 from October 18 to November 3, 2025. Six models, Qwen 3 Max, DeepSeek v3.1, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Grok 4, each got $10,000 to trade crypto perpetuals on Hyperliquid with no human intervention. The organizers set the prompts and rules, and the models chose and placed their own trades.
how_it_went: GNcrypto reports Qwen 3 Max won with about 22% returns, and DeepSeek was the only other model to make a profit. GPT-5 did worst, ending with around $3,733.
worth_knowing: Nof1 founder Jay Azhang said the models were given only numerical time series data, which LLMs don't handle well, plus a constrained set of assets and limited actions. He also saw consistent biases that persisted across many prompt iterations.
prompt: Act as a paper-trading agent for [asset list] using [data source]. Each [interval], review recent price data, decide whether to open, close or hold a position within a simulated balance of [starting amount], and log each decision with a short rationale. Do not place real trades or move any money. At the end of [test period], summarize performance, drawdowns and any recurring biases in your decisions. Show me your trading rules and logging format first and wait for my approval before starting.
